For prediction from text, valid conclusions require no training leakage, meaning no overlap between the model's training data and the research sample, which careful model choice and research design can ensure. For estimation, where LLMs measure economic concepts for downstream analysis, outputs must be combined with a small validation sample to give consistent and precise estimates. Seemingly minor choices, such as the model or prompt, can change parameter estimates dramatically.

entries.title: Generative Brand Choice
entries.tldr: Asks how to predict demand for new products in categories where brand drives choice and observed attributes explain little. Estimates preferences for existing brands with a structural demand model, then fine tunes an LLM to map text descriptions of brands and consumers to those preferences. The tuned LLM generalizes to brands left out of training, with 25% lower mean squared error and a correlation of 0.34 with held out preferences, while text embedding models give zero or negative correlation. Adding instrumental variables price estimates enables pricing counterfactuals.

entries.authors: Xu, Shirong, and Will Wei Sun
entries.title: Do More Predictions Improve Statistical Inference? Filtered Prediction-Powered Inference
entries.tldr: Asks whether using all available AI predictions always helps prediction powered inference. When prediction quality varies, unreliable predictions can dilute useful signal. Proposes Filtered Prediction-Powered Inference (FPPI), which estimates a region where predictions are informative and applies the correction from predictions only there. The estimated region converges quickly under a margin condition, FPPI is asymptotically more efficient than existing methods, and it reduces the need for costly labels in simulations and an LLM evaluation application.

entries.title: Using LLM-Based Priors to Optimize Choice Designs in Conjoint Experiments
entries.tldr: Uses LLMs not as synthetic respondents but as a source of prior part-worth utilities for designing choice-based conjoint experiments before data collection. A study of premium job search platform subscriptions with 984 US job seekers compares a randomized design with designs optimized on aggregate, individualized and deliberately misspecified LLM priors. LLM priors alone predict holdout choices better than chance and, when used to screen out dominated choice tasks, substantially improve prediction, while adding them to Bayesian estimation gives mixed gains.

entries.authors: Harper, F. Maxwell, and Joseph A. Konstan
entries.title: The MovieLens Datasets: History and Context
entries.venue: ACM Transactions on Interactive Intelligent Systems 5(4): Article 19
entries.data_desc: MovieLens 32M: 32M movie ratings from 200,948 users, plus tags.
entries.tldr: Describes the history of the MovieLens datasets, which record member activity on the MovieLens movie recommendation system, a live research platform running since 1997. The datasets are downloaded hundreds of thousands of times each year and are widely used in education, research, and industry. Discusses lessons from running a live research platform over many years and documents best practices and limitations for using the datasets in new research.

entries.title: KuaiRec: A Fully-Observed Dataset and Insights for Evaluating Recommender Systems
entries.data_desc: Short-video watch feedback, dense user-item data, and video metadata.
entries.tldr: Asks how partial observation in logged data distorts offline evaluation of recommender systems. Introduces KuaiRec, collected from Kuaishou, in which almost all of 1,411 users were exposed to each of 3,327 items, described as the first real fully observed dataset, with millions of interactions. A study of multi round conversational recommendation shows that method rankings change with data density and exposure bias, and that imputing missing interactions for user simulation helps only in some cases.

entries.title: KuaiRand: An Unbiased Sequential Recommendation Dataset with Randomly Exposed Videos
entries.data_desc: Short-video logs with randomized exposures and 12 feedback signals.
entries.tldr: Addresses exposure bias in logged recommender data by releasing KuaiRand, a sequential recommendation dataset with millions of interactions on videos randomly inserted into feeds of the Kuaishou app over two weeks. Unlike earlier randomized datasets such as Yahoo!, Coat and OpenBandit, which are small or lack user IDs and features, it records 12 kinds of feedback, such as clicks, likes and view time, plus rich user and item features and behavior histories. It supports debiasing research at scale, along with interactive recommendation, long sequence modeling and multitask learning.

entries.title: Human vs. Agent in Task-Oriented Conversations
entries.data_desc: RecLLMSim: human and LLM recommendation dialogues with profiles and annotations.
entries.tldr: Compares LLM-simulated users with human users in personalized task-oriented conversations. Proposes a framework covering conversation strategy, interaction style and conversation evaluation, with ten dimensions of user behavior, and collects parallel datasets of human and LLM agent users across four scenarios. Simulated and human users differ significantly in problem solving approach, question breadth, engagement, feedback and language style, while agreeing on some dimensions. The findings are meant to guide how user simulation is used in conversational systems.

categories.blurb: algorithm performance, synthetic training signals, and improved learning methods

intro: A curated list of papers on large language models (LLMs) for marketing, organized around consumer simulation, content generation and personalization, and model and algorithm augmentation. The collection prioritizes marketing research, with selected computer-science and social-science methods, validation studies, and reviews.
